clue.text: Cake Rubens represented having risen badly, current missing in heaters

indicators.note: to be represented anew is to be presented in another form, so the painter's name is rearranged
done badly suggests a botched order, so the word before it is jumbled
a current that is missing has been taken out of the word it would sit in

blocks.note: a bun is a small cake
the Flemish painter's name, taken as written to be rearranged
taken as written before losing a letter
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A baker's cake, decorated in the manner of Rubens, has risen badly because the electricity failed in the ovens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current missing' applies only to the second word: the I for electric current goes before it is jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunsen burners are the gas flames used in laboratories, so they are one kind of heating device.

clue.text: Express disapproval about Latin grammar: not advisable, initially, somewhere in Italy

indicators.note: about means around, so the jeer is wrapped round the next letter
initially points to the opening letter of each word in the phrase it follows

blocks.note: to boo is to express disapproval
L is the standard abbreviation for Latin
G is an abbreviation for grammar
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A teacher tuts at a lesson on Latin grammar, warning against travelling somewhere in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: BO(L)O + G + NA gives the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bologna is a historic university city in northern Italy, capital of the Emilia-Romagna region.

clue.text: I complain about old mother-in-law

indicators.note: about here means turned about, so the phrase before it is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to moan is to complain

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about their elderly mother-in-law.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Old Testament Book of Ruth, Naomi is Ruth's mother-in-law, which is why she is 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is the biblical woman whose widowed daughter-in-law Ruth stayed loyally with her.

clue.text: Beethoven's fifth concerto describing a kind of penguin

blocks.note: first meaning: the nickname of Beethoven's Piano Concerto No 5
second meaning: the largest species of penguin, from Antarctica

explanation.surface: A music critic finds Beethoven's grand concerto evokes a dignified penguin.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth piano concerto carries the nickname Emperor, and the biggest Antarctic penguin species shares that name.

clue.text: A tribesman began to crumple, having been knocked down

indicators.note: something that crumples loses its shape, so the phrase's letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warrior starts to collapse after being struck to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked down' looks like a blow in a fight, but it means reduced in price.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are knocked down are sold cheaply, and bargain-basement describes very low-priced merchandise.

clue.text: Greek island which will lead, they say, to Italian city

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is heard rather than read

blocks.clueFragment: which will lead, they say, to Italian city
blocks.note: the proverb says all roads lead to Rome, the Italian city

explanation.surface: A travel guide claims a Greek island is the route to Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'all roads lead to Rome' supplies the word that is pronounced like the island's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is the largest of the Dodecanese islands in the Aegean, famous for its ancient Colossus.

clue.text: Everyman’s shown up with drunken English lords and sinners

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, so the contraction runs backwards
a drunken person staggers about, so the letters that follow lurch out of order

blocks.note: the setter Everyman speaks as I, and Everyman's means Everyman has, so I've
E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written to be rearranged with the E

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to appearing alongside tipsy English aristocrats and other ne'er-do-wells.
explanation.walkthrough: Everyman's stands for 'I've' (I have), the setter speaking of himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Evildoers are people who commit wicked acts, which makes them wrongdoers in a moral sense.

clue.text: Spare part installed by artisan after losing first four

indicators.note: losing the first four means dropping the opening four letters of the craftsman word
something installed is fitted inside, so this word goes within the shortened one

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written before its first four letters go

explanation.surface: A mechanic fits a spare part, though the craftsman has lost his first four attempts.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTISAN without ARTI leaves SAN, which holds PART: S(PART)AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare and Spartan both describe something austere and frugal, with no comforts or luxuries.

clue.text: Primarily, clever lyrist inhabiting Olympus?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the opening letter of each following word

blocks.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A gifted poet lives on Mount Olympus.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a description of a Muse, one of the goddesses of the arts who dwell on Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: Clio is one of the nine Muses, the Greek goddesses of inspiration who lived with the gods.

clue.text: Time, perhaps, for every one old to call about cold

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for call goes around the temperature letter

blocks.note: per means for each or for every
I is the Roman numeral one
O is a standard abbreviation for old
to dial is to call on the telephone
C stands for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is time for each elderly person to phone about a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: PER + I + O + DI(C)AL. 'Time' wants to be a duration; it is the news magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is a weekly news magazine, an example of a publication issued at regular intervals.

clue.text: Queen’s after exotic fruit: that’s increasingly plain

blocks.note: the ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: The Queen is chasing some exotic fruit, which looks less attractive the longer it sits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen's after' means ER follows the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain describes an unattractive face, so more and more plain is the comparative of ugly.

clue.text: Account involving narrative, extremely droll, one tells everyone for starters?

definitions.text: Account involving narrative, extremely droll, one tells everyone

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the abbreviation wraps around the next two letters
starters are the opening items, so each word contributes its initial letter

blocks.note: AC, or a/c, is the abbreviation for account
the first letters of these two words
the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A funny story you tell to everyone is a narrative of a particularly droll kind.
explanation.walkthrough: A(NE)C + DOTE. The whole clue also describes the answer: a short amusing tale told to all.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short entertaining story about a real incident, typically told to amuse listeners.

clue.text: Oarsman flailing about in landlocked country

indicators.note: flailing arms move wildly, so the rower's letters thrash into a new order
about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the small word

blocks.note: taken as written to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rower thrashes about helplessly in a country with no coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged rower, SANMARO, goes around IN. The joke is a rower stranded where there is no sea.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny republic entirely surrounded by Italy, so it has no coastline.

clue.text: One armed with sword (in fiction) and firearm (in reality)!

definitions.text: One armed with sword (in fiction) and firearm (in reality)!

blocks.note: surface reading: a fictional swordsman, such as Dumas's heroes Athos, Porthos and Aramis
setter's reading: the historical soldiers were named after the early gun they carried, not a blade

explanation.walkthrough: Dumas's famous trio fight with swords, yet their real-life namesakes were infantry carrying an early long gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A musketeer was a soldier armed with a musket, though fiction made them famous as swordsmen.

clue.text: Christmas in retirement in Spanish kingdom

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the festive word is read backwards

blocks.note: Noel is another word for Christmas

explanation.surface: Someone spends the Christmas holidays retired in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: León was a medieval kingdom of north-west Spain, later united with Castile.

clue.text: Give medicine to those in Brooklyn

indicators.note: in Brooklyn means spoken with a New York accent, where th sounds become d

blocks.note: a stereotypical Brooklyn accent says 'those' with a hard d at the start

explanation.surface: A New York pharmacist hands out medicine to particular people.
explanation.walkthrough: Brooklyn speech famously turns 'th' into 'd', as in 'dem' and 'dose'.
explanation.definitionFit: To dose someone is to administer a measured quantity of a drug to them.

clue.text: A bit of Poldark we bit-torrented in lawless online world

indicators.note: a bit of means only a portion, so the letters lie within the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the TV drama's name into the next words

explanation.surface: Someone illegally downloaded an episode of the TV drama Poldark using a torrent site.
explanation.walkthrough: Poldark is a BBC period drama set in Cornwall; bit-torrenting is file-sharing, often of pirated shows.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark web is the hidden part of the internet, reached through special software, where illegal trade flourishes.

clue.text: Distressed damsel in Alfa Romeo

indicators.note: distressed means upset, so the letters that follow are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written to be rearranged
taken as written
Alfa is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for the letter A

explanation.surface: A damsel in distress is riding in an Italian sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alfa Romeo' looks like the car marque, but it splits: Alfa for A, Romeo as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romeo, after Shakespeare's lover, is a man who woos many women, a charming womaniser.

clue.text: Tooth seen in bionic bits you’re oddly ignoring

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones in the phrase

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and so on letters of these words

explanation.surface: A dentist spots a tooth among the robotic parts of a cyborg's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisor is one of the sharp front teeth used for cutting food.

clue.text: Relaxing, Bambi? Entirely? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the preceding words is used

blocks.note: the letters span the deer's name and the next word

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether watching Bambi is completely restful, and answers that it is not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the clue's own words, 'not entirely', answer its question and tell you to take only part of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes soothing atmospheric music designed to calm the listener, so it suits a restful mood.

clue.text: A little classic board game getting to grips with homicide, in the end?

definitions.text: A little classic board game getting to grips with homicide, in the end?

indicators.note: a little of the word means just its first letter
gripping something means holding it inside, so the game surrounds a letter
the end of the killing word is its last letter

blocks.note: the first letter of classic
Ludo is a classic dice-and-counter board game
the last letter of homicide

explanation.surface: A small classic board game that ultimately grapples with murder.
explanation.walkthrough: C + LU(E)DO. Read whole, the clue describes the murder-mystery game itself; Ludo is the British name for Parcheesi.
explanation.definitionFit: Cluedo, known as Clue in North America, is the classic board game of solving a murder.

clue.text: A Spandau Ballet song, a Joni Mitchell song and a Madonna song

blocks.note: True was Spandau Ballet's 1983 hit
Blue is the title track of Joni Mitchell's 1971 album

explanation.surface: A playlist of three pop songs from different artists.
explanation.walkthrough: The two song titles joined give the third.
explanation.definitionFit: True Blue was Madonna's 1986 hit single and the title track of her third album.

clue.text: Cry-baby mostly unsettled and grouchy

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the final letter is dropped
unsettled means disturbed, so the remaining letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written before being cut

explanation.surface: A whining child, mostly upset and bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby means irritable and bad-tempered, the same sense as being in a grumpy mood.

clue.text: American shiraz technician bottles

indicators.note: to bottle is to hold inside, so the phrase contains the letters wanted

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the wine and the start of the job

explanation.surface: A winery technician in the United States bottles shiraz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' looks like it describes the technician, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were the Native American people who ruled central Mexico before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Bribes ‘small, insubstantial’: low-value banknotes with one note missing

indicators.note: one note missing means a single N, the abbreviation for note, is dropped

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
wee, Scottish for tiny, means slight or insubstantial
tenners are British ten-pound notes, the lowest common denominations

explanation.surface: Kickbacks are dismissed as minor, just a few low notes with one missing.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is a British ten-pound note; one of its two Ns goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is an inducement or bribe given to win someone over to a deal.

clue.text: We're told drawing of the sea ... is ... drawn

indicators.note: we're told means we hear it said, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: the moon draws the sea in and out

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly reports that a picture of the ocean has been sketched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' and 'drawn' look like art, but one is the moon's pull on the sea and the other a level score.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn match ends level, and a game that is tied finishes with equal scores.

clue.text: Writer spending energy once in novel, Torch, Belt & Beret

indicators.note: spending means using up, so the energy symbol is removed from the fodder
once means a single time, so only one of the several energy symbols is taken away
novel means new, so the listed items are made into a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author's novel is titled like a list of kit: a torch, a belt and a beret.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the three Es in TORCH, BELT and BERET is dropped, which is what 'once' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertolt Brecht was the German playwright and poet who wrote Mother Courage and The Threepenny Opera.
